tasks.short: Agree advertising placements with media partners, deliver approved materials, and confirm publication.

steps.what: Collect the campaign brief, approved assets, budget, and placement schedule.
Exchange specifications, availability, deadlines, and missing information with media partners.

loop.input: Media correspondence and media specifications for one placement.
loop.output: Draft placement requirements and unresolved questions with source references.
loop.check: Validate dates, dimensions, formats, and quoted terms; manager confirms ambiguous requirements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per thread update; unresolved fields return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Partners describe requirements in varied prose and attachments; structured forms cover only some partners.

steps.what: Resolve placement changes, timing conflicts, and relationship concerns with the media partner.
Check final materials, claims, destinations, and placement terms before authorizing release.
Send approved files and instructions, then obtain delivery acknowledgement.
Compare publication evidence with the agreement and resolve missing or incorrect placements.

tasks.design: A generator assembles versioned placement packs from {DOCS} and {PROJECT}; a bounded loop turns correspondence from {EMAIL} into requirements for review. A configured {WORKFLOW} checks completeness, captures release approval, and sends only the approved asset version to the approved recipient. Delivery receipts and publication evidence feed a placement queue in {PROJECT}, where the manager handles disputes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Partner formats differ, asset versions drift, and agreements live in correspondence. Coordination also depends on trust and informal commitments.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard forms, document links, and configured approvals already handle much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building pack generators; bounded extraction handles varied correspondence.
tasks.still_hard: Publication evidence may be screenshots or print copies. Placement quality, late changes, and partner disputes still need people.
tasks.human_edge: The manager secures cooperation, protects the relationship, and judges when a placement change damages the campaign.

ambition.what: A placement assurance service that flags missing publication evidence before invoice approval.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer file searches and delivery chasers, with more attention to placement quality and partner exceptions. Existing negotiation and release limits remain; additional commercial authority requires explicit delegation.

reach.task: Coordinate publication timing across paid advertising and press activity.
reach.learn: Learn embargo handling, editorial deadlines, and the distinction between paid placement and editorial coverage.

evidence.claim: Configured publishing and campaign workflows are available today; bespoke media-partner coordination remains an extension.
Pack generation, reviewed correspondence extraction, and approval-controlled delivery are feasible engineering patterns.
The digest documents API-linked follow-up automation, but provides no case for this complete media-placement workflow.
AI Act Article 50 transparency duties need assessment when advertising uses synthetic content.

assumptions: Time shares describe a typical placement cycle, including routine coordination and occasional corrections.
The communication-heavy prior is retained; automation targets preparation, requirement capture, and delivery.
Delivery is limited to an approved recipient, asset version, and placement; changed terms reopen approval.
Build ranges are estimates for one placement workflow with existing document and email access.
Access estimates include employee consultation under national rules if the implementation introduces staff monitoring.
unknowns: Which media partners accept structured requirements, uploads, or delivery APIs?
Where are final assets, claim approvals, and placement agreements stored?
Who can authorize release and agree commercial changes?
What publication evidence is available, and who approves related invoices?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing {WORKFLOW} configuration capture approval against an immutable asset version?
Which partner interfaces provide reliable delivery and publication receipts?
How accurately can the extraction loop identify changed deadlines and specifications in representative correspondence?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and unresolved questions.
Maintain recipient permissions, specification templates, and delivery rules.
Handle failed deliveries and missing publication evidence.
Maintain synthetic-content disclosure checks where applicable.

tasks.short: Discuss advertising products, media choices, and contract constraints with department heads and staff.

steps.what: Gather campaign results, product priorities, contract constraints, and budget options into a briefing.
Arrange the discussion and circulate the briefing and questions.
Discuss trade-offs, clarify constraints, and work through disagreements with department heads and staff.
Write the decision summary, unresolved issues, and proposed actions.

loop.input: Discussion notes and proposed decision, without assuming meeting recording.
loop.output: Draft decision summary and actions with owners, dates, and unresolved issues.
loop.check: Trace each decision to notes; manager verifies attribution and separates proposals from approvals.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per meeting; unclear commitments remain explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion notes express decisions and reservations in free text; templates alone cannot interpret them.

steps.what: Approve the selected product, media direction, or expenditure within delegated authority.
Assign approved actions and update the campaign plan.

tasks.design: A generator builds a sourced decision brief from {BI}, {ERP}, and approved records in {DOCS}, while {CALENDAR} and {WORKFLOW} arrange the discussion. A bounded loop drafts the decision summary from notes for manager review. Department-head approval activates the agreed actions in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation spans several sources, while the discussion depends on competing priorities and informal context. Meeting notes often blur proposals and final decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable brief templates and existing scheduling features remove routine preparation. A bounded drafting loop can organize notes without taking over the discussion.
tasks.still_hard: People may withhold concerns, change priorities, or disagree about authority. Source records cannot capture every political or commercial constraint.
tasks.human_edge: The manager draws out objections, builds agreement, and recognizes when apparent consensus is fragile.

ambition.what: A fortnightly decision session for stalled product-promotion choices.

tasks.altitude: More preparation arrives ready to inspect, leaving time for difficult conversations and follow-through. The manager can frame options more clearly; approval rights remain with the existing decision makers.

reach.task: Translate product priorities into an agreed campaign portfolio.
reach.learn: Learn contribution margins, positioning choices, and how competing campaigns affect shared budgets.

evidence.claim: Template-generated briefings, configured approvals, and reviewed note drafting are feasible; no task-specific case is supplied.
Campaign-plan drafting is commercially available, supporting preparation rather than delegated organizational decisions.

assumptions: The meeting remains the largest time share, consistent with the human-conversation prior.
Brief inputs are approved structured records or links; the generator exposes missing inputs rather than inventing them.
Discussion notes are available; recording and transcription are outside the initial scope.
Build ranges cover one briefing template and one approval route.
Consultation under national rules is assessed if meeting-data collection or staff monitoring expands.
unknowns: Which decisions require department-head, finance, or legal approval?
Are campaign results and budgets available through governed exports or APIs?
How are decisions and action ownership recorded today?
Which confidential information can each participant access?
Which national employee-consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can existing {PROJECT} and {WORKFLOW} configuration distinguish proposed actions from approved actions?
Does note drafting preserve reservations and distinguish agreement from discussion in representative meetings?
new_work: Review draft summaries and correct attribution.
Maintain briefing templates and source permissions.
Resolve missing owners, deadlines, and approval ambiguity.
Keep decision records aligned with subsequent changes.

tasks.short: Combine marketing and sales data with market context to forecast demand and campaign conditions.

steps.what: Retrieve channel results, sales history, pipeline, budgets, and market reports.
Align periods, channel names, currencies, and definitions; investigate missing or inconsistent figures.
Calculate trends, seasonal patterns, baseline forecasts, and alternative scenarios.
Read market reports and campaign notes for changes the historical baseline misses.

loop.input: Selected dated market reports and campaign notes alongside the baseline forecast.
loop.output: Sourced change signals, contradictions, and suggested assumptions for review.
loop.check: Require source passages and dates; reject unsupported numeric effects and separate observations from hypotheses.
loop.stop: One pass over the selected source set and one repair; missing evidence returns to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports describe market shifts in varied prose; keywords cannot reliably distinguish evidence from speculation.

steps.what: Challenge assumptions with sales and finance, then approve the forecast interpretation.
Prepare the forecast report with scenarios, assumptions, uncertainty, and recommended campaign responses.
Distribute the report and record when its assumptions should be revisited.

tasks.design: Configured feeds bring {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, {CRM}, and {ERP} data into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, where deterministic checks and statistical forecasts produce scenarios in {BI}. A bounded loop reads selected reports from {DOCS} and proposes sourced context for manager review. Approval fixes the forecast version, after which a generator publishes the report; budget changes require their existing approvals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channel definitions differ, historical data needs cleaning, and forecast spreadsheets are hard to reproduce. Market changes also require interpretation beyond historical patterns.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and statistical methods handle collection and baseline forecasting. AI-assisted coding makes validation and report generation cheaper; bounded reading reduces the cost of reviewing qualitative context.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution, sparse history, structural market shifts, and missing consented data limit forecast quality. Faster calculations do not establish causal advertising effects.
tasks.human_edge: The manager recognizes when historical relationships have broken and chooses which commercial assumptions deserve a test.

ambition.what: A weekly demand-risk review that selects one campaign hypothesis to test.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling monthly figures to reviewing forecast errors and choosing campaign tests. The manager gains a more frequent basis for recommendations; test-spend authority depends on an agreed delegation.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Design a campaign experiment that separates demand changes from advertising effects.
reach.learn: Learn holdout design, sampling bias, uncertainty intervals, and causal interpretation.

reach.task: Translate forecast scenarios into channel test plans.
reach.learn: Learn conversion lag, attribution limits, and channel-specific response curves.

evidence.claim: Marketing connectors, standardized channel data, automated reporting, and marketing mix modelling are available today.
CRM-based deal probability and revenue-forecast assistance are available; this does not prove demand-forecast accuracy.
Statistical baselines, rolling backtests, and versioned scenario reports are established engineering patterns.
Consent requirements constrain the availability of non-essential tracking data.
An objection to direct marketing also covers related profiling and must be respected.

assumptions: Data preparation is automatable, but the judgement-heavy prior limits automation of final interpretation.
The initial forecast uses aggregate campaign and sales data and does not evaluate individual employees.
Forecast methods are selected through rolling backtests against a simple baseline.
Invalid or stale source data prevents report release and creates an exception.
Build estimates cover a limited channel set and sufficient historical data for backtesting.
Consultation under national rules is assessed if the scope later introduces employee monitoring.
unknowns: How much consistent historical data is available?
Which channel, revenue, and conversion definitions are authoritative?
Are tracking permissions and direct-marketing objections reflected in source systems?
Which forecast horizon matters, and what error would change a campaign decision?
Who approves the forecast and any resulting spend changes?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed data use?
research_questions: Which existing connectors preserve revisions, currency treatment, and source timestamps?
Which baseline performs best on representative historical periods?
How should forecasts behave during stock shortages, major promotions, or structural market changes?
Can the report generator expose uncertainty without implying unsupported precision?
new_work: Investigate data-quality exceptions and changed metric definitions.
Review sourced market signals and proposed assumptions.
Track forecast errors, drift, and baseline performance.
Maintain connectors, backtests, access controls, and report templates.
Document campaign tests and compare results with forecast assumptions.

tasks.short: Prepare advertising or sales contract drafts, negotiate terms, obtain approvals, and arrange signature.

steps.what: Collect the commercial brief, counterparty details, proposed terms, and approval limits.
Populate the approved contract template and attach the commercial schedule.
Review counterparty edits and identify commercial or legal departures from the draft.

loop.input: Document comparison, counterparty redline, approved clause library, and approval matrix.
loop.output: Draft deviation register with clause references and issues for negotiation or legal review.
loop.check: Reconcile against deterministic text differences; quote changed clauses and verify amounts and dates separately.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair per version; unknown clauses or unreadable text go to legal counsel.
loop.why_not_simpler: Text comparison finds edits but cannot reliably interpret varied clause wording or cross-clause consequences.

steps.what: Negotiate price, scope, rights, deadlines, cancellation terms, and remedies with the counterparty.
Review legal departures and approve or return the contract for revision.
Approve the commercial commitment against budget and delegated authority.
Check the final approved version and sign through the signature process.
File the signed contract and record obligations, payment milestones, and renewal dates.

tasks.design: A configured intake in {WORKFLOW} pulls counterparty details from {CRM} or {PROCUREMENT}, and a deterministic generator fills approved templates in {DOCS}. Document comparison plus a bounded loop prepares a sourced deviation register; people negotiate and approve legal and commercial terms. Version-bound approvals control the signature process in {ESIGN}, then populate contract records and obligation reminders in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commercial details arrive incompletely, templates drift, and redlines require interpretation. Negotiations and approval authority cannot be reduced to document generation.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, template assembly, document comparison, and signature workflows already exist. AI-assisted coding reduces integration effort, while bounded clause classification helps reviewers focus their attention.
tasks.still_hard: Non-standard liability, intellectual-property rights, sales commitments, and cross-border terms need specialist judgement. Scanned documents and late changes complicate version control.
tasks.human_edge: The manager reads bargaining signals and trades concessions without damaging the commercial relationship; legal counsel judges acceptable legal exposure.

ambition.what: A pre-negotiation options brief showing approved concession packages and their commercial consequences.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time copying terms and comparing versions, and more time preparing concessions and negotiating. Signing and approval rights remain unchanged unless the organization explicitly delegates a wider commercial envelope.

reach.task: Assess the margin and delivery consequences of proposed promotional commitments.
reach.learn: Learn contribution economics, fulfillment constraints, and how concessions affect the campaign business case.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, deterministic contract assembly, version-bound approvals, and signature routing are feasible patterns.
Bounded redline classification can assist review, but the digest supplies no contract-specific product evidence or documented case.

assumptions: Advertising and sales contracts use separate templates and approval routes within the same contracting workflow.
For sales contracts, the budget owner represents the role authorized to approve commercial exposure.
The conversation-heavy prior is retained; contract paperwork and review preparation provide most of the time savings.
At least some approved templates and clause positions are available.
Only approved structured terms populate obligations automatically; bespoke obligations remain review items.
Build estimates cover two template families and existing signature access.
Access work includes GDPR requirements and consultation under national rules where employee-data use requires it.
unknowns: What proportion of contracts use approved templates rather than counterparty paper?
Are approved clauses, concession limits, and escalation routes documented?
Which roles can negotiate, approve deviations, and sign?
Are contracts digitally readable, and where is the authoritative version stored?
Does a {CLM} already provide intake, assembly, comparison, and obligation tracking?
Which national contract and employee-consultation rules apply?
research_questions: Can existing {CLM} configuration replace the proposed custom generator or workflow?
How well does deviation classification detect consequential edits in representative contract versions?
Can signature routing enforce approval against the exact final document version?
Which bespoke obligations require explicit human confirmation before scheduling?
new_work: Review flagged deviations and correct missed or misclassified clauses.
Maintain approved templates, clause positions, and concession limits.
Resolve incomplete intake and unmatched counterparty records.
Test version binding after document or signature-system changes.
Review bespoke obligations and update reminders after amendments.

role.altitude: The advertising manager's week shifts toward partner negotiation, campaign choices, forecast interpretation, and contract trade-offs. Better preparation supports more frequent decisions; new spending, signing, or publishing authority still requires explicit delegation.
reach: Marketing Managers: connect campaign choices and contract concessions to contribution margins and product priorities.
Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists: turn forecast uncertainty into credible campaign experiments.
Search Marketing Strategists: translate demand scenarios into channel tests while accounting for conversion lag.
Public Relations Specialists: coordinate paid placement timing with press activity and embargoes.
skills_to_grow: Read forecast diagnostics and distinguish correlation from causal effects.
Design campaign tests with useful uncertainty and stopping criteria.
Prepare concession packages and understand contract risk.
Validate sourced model outputs and recognize unresolved ambiguity.
Use approval limits, document versions, and data permissions correctly.
Facilitate decisions across conflicting departmental priorities.
role.ambitious_version: Run a weekly campaign decision service that combines demand-risk scenarios, placement assurance, and pre-negotiation options. People retain commercial judgement, relationship work, and approval of binding commitments.
